verifications.note: FERC's notice of UGI Sunbury's application (full text at federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/text/2015/07/21/2015-17810.txt): the company sought "a certificate authorizing Sunbury to construct, own, and operate new INTERSTATE natural gas pipeline facilities (Sunbury Pipeline Project)" under NGA section 7(c) — the FERC-jurisdictional certificate class that defines an interstate transmission pipeline, as opposed to a gathering or local-distribution line.

"The Sunbury Pipeline...is a federally-regulated 35-mile, 20-inch pipeline...Sunbury Pipeline interconnects to other pipelines including Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company ('Transco'), Marc I Pipeline..." — federally-regulated interstate interconnection with two other interstate transmission systems.

resolutions.researcher_notes: PipelineType='transmission' is not printed as the literal word on either page, but is stated by definition: FERC's own notice classifies the line as an interstate natural-gas pipeline under NGA 7(c) (the transmission-pipeline certificate class), and the operator's site confirms federal (not state/local) regulation plus direct interconnection with two named interstate transmission systems (Transco, MARC I). Treated the same way the SOP treats status-by-inference: the classification is entailed by the prose even though the token 'transmission' never appears verbatim.

Searched for a second, independent naming of Marcellus as the source gas: checked the FERC notice of application (federalregister.gov/2015-17810 full text) — no mention of Marcellus, only 'new pipeline capacity'; Hydrocarbons Technology (hydrocarbons-technology.com, wayback) — describes 'low-cost natural gas' but never names Marcellus specifically; RBN Energy (rbnenergy.com/node/5296, wayback) — 'Commodity: Natural Gas' with no shale-play field populated; Pipeline & Gas Journal (pgjonline.com, wayback preview) and Electric Energy Online — neither mentions Marcellus in the available text; ugies.com (UGI Energy Services corporate site) and fractracker.org's Feb-2020 petrochemical-map page — neither names Marcellus in connection with this pipeline specifically. UGI's own /overview/ subpage (web.archive.org/web/2018id_/http://sunburypipeline.com/overview/) also states Marcellus sourcing but is the same operator/domain as the primary ref, so not counted as independent. No second, differently-sourced confirmation found; not adding a fabricated one.

resolutions.researcher_notes: SegmentCost=178,000,000 USD matches, within rounding, UGI Sunbury's own FERC-filed cost estimate of $178,243,345 (primary/regulatory source, so filled at medium rather than left blank though only one source matches this exact figure). FLAGGING A DISCREPANCY FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: RBN Energy's database (web.archive.org/web/2019id_/https://rbnenergy.com/node/5296) lists a different, lower figure — "Est Capital Cost: $160 Million" — about $18M (10%) below both the FERC estimate and the recorded sheet value. Not treated as corroboration (it disagrees, not agrees) and not proposed as a ref for this reason; worth a look at whether $160M reflects a later as-built/actual figure vs. FERC's pre-construction estimate, but the recorded $178M is the one directly traceable to a primary filed source.
